A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DITS research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures. Renamed, relocated and reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original DITS experiments across eight datasets, including training results, data-selection ablations, synthesis-budget experiments and iterative-training analyses. Baseline results attributed to earlier work are distinguishable from these original results.

after.justification: v2 retains original DITS results and adds WebWalker evaluation, computational-cost measurements, validation-set experiments and evaluations with additional base models.

M1.justification: Equation (5) changes the reported Q-value update from averaging child-node Q-values to averaging rewards over trajectories containing the node. These weight branches differently when rollout counts differ. The influence estimator, combined selection score, filtering rules and iterative SFT/DPO procedure otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates eight datasets across Information Exchange and Debate. v2 retains six, removes MATH and GSM8k, and adds WebWalker under DeepSearch. DeepSearch introduces dynamic collaboration among three agents performing web search and content analysis, substantially extending the evaluated input environment and task requirements.

E2.justification: The retained static experiments preserve their comparator sets. New Table 2 evaluates Direct Reasoning, RAG Workflow and its query-planning and iterative variants, Search-o1, and WebThinker-based configurations. Table 5 additionally compares DITS analytically with TRAK and LESS using estimated computational costs; it does not establish empirical training comparisons with those methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include QwQ-32B for DeepSearch, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct answer judging and retrieval of ten search results. Additional experiments vary synthesis budgets, sample counts and validation sizes, and evaluate Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Retained static hyperparameters are unchanged; the newly stated default validation size is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: v2 adds validation-size sensitivity, validation-set robustness, comparisons between high/low-Q and high/low-influence selections, computational-efficiency analyses and cross-model testing. The mathematics-specific distribution analyses disappear. Existing selection-ratio, iterative-training and case-study analyses are largely retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix G.3 and Table 7 newly report five training outcomes obtained using different 20-example validation sets, providing limited evidence of variability from validation sampling. v1 has no analogous replication report. Neither version provides seed identifiers, confidence intervals or significance tests for the main benchmark comparisons.

E6.justification: Shared entries in v1 Tables 1–2 and v2 Tables 1 and 3 are unchanged, while MATH and GSM8k results are removed. New results include WebWalker scores of 47.2 for DITS-DPO versus 46.6 for Optima-DPO, cost and selection comparisons, validation-set scores spanning 61.8–62.4, and additional base-model results. These are added experimental findings, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: New Appendix B defines group-weighted training and uses an additive first-order influence approximation to argue that selecting the most influential examples maximizes validation performance. Appendix F adds computational-cost derivations. v2 also revises the Q-value definition in Equation (5) and removes v1's explicit Hessian-based influence formula. The new selection argument relies on approximation rather than an unconditional guarantee.

C1.justification: The central contributions—influence-based selection, efficient estimation for non-differentiable metrics and iterative improvement—remain. The abstract and introduction revise the empirical scope to seven datasets across three tasks, explicitly including DeepSearch. The introduction changes the claimed single-round improvement from 2.1% to 2.7% and adds a 2.6% DeepSearch improvement claim.

C2.justification: v2 explains when Q-values can complement noisy influence estimates, interprets high-Q/low-influence examples as risking overfitting, and discusses validation accuracy versus computational cost. Its new limitations section excludes dynamic agent spawning and emergent teams from the evaluated scope and identifies latency constraints on real-time use. Earlier mathematics-specific interpretations are removed with those experiments.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer, explicitly discloses the default 20-example validation set, describes DeepSearch models and search configuration, and reports GPU-hour accounting. Existing LoRA, filtering and retained-dataset training hyperparameters largely persist. These are useful additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for WebThinker, Search-o1, WebWalker, Llama 3 and Qwen, and removes references associated with the discarded mathematics evaluations. Related work newly describes MALT as a special case of Optima. The broader positioning relative to Optima, MATES and influence-function research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Appendix A, the algorithm moves to Appendix C, and iterative-performance discussion moves to Appendix G.1. Dataset descriptions also move into an appendix. The abstract, introduction and conclusion are revised, and a dedicated limitations section replaces the earlier closing structure containing an impact statement.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, caption formatting and appendix layout, and adds several experimental tables and a validation-size figure. It merges v1 Figures 4 and 6 into Figure 4, moves the CBT distribution panel into Figure 3, and redraws and relocates the iteration radar plot without the mathematics axes. Existing tables also lose mathematics columns.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence supporting DITS through explicit total-cost accounting in Table 4 and validation-set reliability tests in Appendix G.3. Additional model evaluations, concrete applicability limits and a code pointer improve assessment and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of mathematics coverage, but the new cost and validation analyses concentrate on 2WMH QA, and the theoretical optimality argument depends on assumed additivity. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
